problems.title: Directions in a regular hexagon
problems.question: Find the angle between lines EF and CD of regular hexagon ABCDEF.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Exterior turn $=360°/6=60°$; the angle between lines is at most 90°.
steps: Successive side directions turn by 60°. CD and EF differ by two turns, or 120° as directed sides; their smaller line angle is 60°.
problems.note: This source is the Quiz 3 retake, dated 28 March 2022, and is printed Variant I.

problems.title: Express powers with one base
problems.question: Solve 0.4^(2x−1)=2.5^x.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: $0.4=2.5^{-1}$; equal powers of a positive base other than 1 have equal exponents.
steps: Thus 1−2x=x, giving 3x=1.

problems.title: Collinear position vectors
problems.question: O=(0,0),A=(3,5),B=(x+1,x) are collinear. Find OB/OA.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Solving gives x=−5/2 and B=(−3/2,−5/2)=−A/2. Lengths ignore the negative direction, so OB/OA=1/2.

problems.title: Faster travel and time saved
problems.question: For the same distance, the second car is 60% faster. What percentage less time does it take?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: If the first speed is v, the second is 1.6v. Its time is 1/1.6=5/8 of the first time. The saving is 3/8=37.5%.

problems.title: A chord parallel to another chord
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie on a circle with centre O; AC is a diameter, AB∥CD, ABO=30°, CD=2. Find the circle area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: In isosceles AOB, $\angle AOB=120°$; chord length $=2R\sin(\theta/2)$.
steps: Use unit-circle coordinates A=(1,0), B=(−1/2,√3/2), C=(−1,0). The line through C parallel to AB meets the circle at D=(1/2,−√3/2).
Hence CD=√3R=2, so R²=4/3 and area=4π/3.

problems.title: Count the zeros of a product
problems.question: How many real solutions does (x²−9)(x³−64x)(sin x+cos x−6)=0 have?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The first two factors give −3,3 and −8,0,8. The last factor is never zero because 6>√2. There are five distinct roots.

problems.title: The sign of cosine from a quadrant
problems.question: tan x=2 and 90°<x<270°. Find cos x.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Positive tangent in this interval places x in quadrant III. Therefore cosine is negative, and cos x=−1/√5.

problems.title: A minimum at the domain endpoint
problems.question: Find the minimum of 11+fourth-root(x−2)+√(x−6).
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: The common real domain is $x\ge6$; both roots increase with x.
steps: The minimum is at x=6: 11+fourth-root(4)+0=11+√2.

problems.title: How many triangles fit two sides and an angle?
problems.question: Two sides are 4,5 and one angle is 60°. Count noncongruent triangles.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Cosine rule $c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$; sine rule $\sin B/b=\sin A/a$.
steps: If 60° is included between 4 and 5, the third side is √21, giving one triangle.
If 60° is opposite side 4, the angle opposite 5 would have sine 5√3/8>1: impossible.
If 60° is opposite side 5, the angle opposite 4 has sine 2√3/5. Only its acute value works, since its obtuse supplement plus 60° exceeds 180°. This gives one more triangle.

problems.title: Inradius-to-circumradius ratios
problems.question: Order these ratios for a square a, regular hexagon b, and regular octagon c.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The angles are 45°,30°,22.5°. Cosine is larger at the smaller of these angles, so a<b<c.

problems.title: Choose the geometric ratio using a sign
problems.question: A geometric progression has b₁<0, b₅−b₁=15, b₄−b₂=6. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Dividing the two differences gives (q²+1)/q=15/6. Thus 2q²−5q+2=0, giving q=2 or 1/2.
The first difference is b₁(q⁴−1)>0 with b₁<0, so |q|<1. Keep q=1/2.

problems.title: Minimize a quadratic sequence
problems.question: Find the smallest term of aₙ=3n²−23n+1, n=1,2,… .
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Check the nearest integers 3 and 4: a₃=−41 and a₄=−43. The upward-opening quadratic increases away from its vertex.

problems.title: Rectangle perimeter from area and diagonal
problems.question: A rectangle has area 120 and diagonal 17. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Here u²+v²=289 and uv=120, so (u+v)²=529 and u+v=23. Perimeter=46.

problems.title: Locate the other quadratic root
problems.question: One root of 3x²+ax−5=0 lies in (0.6,2). Locate the other.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: As r increases from 3/5 to 2, the negative quantity −5/(3r) increases from −25/9 to −5/6. The endpoints remain excluded.

problems.title: Length of a vector combination
problems.question: |a|=2, |b|=1 and the angle is 120°. Find |2a−3b|.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The dot product is −1. The squared length is 16+9+12=37.

problems.title: A hexagon resting on an axis
problems.question: AF of regular hexagon ABCDEF is on the x-axis; B,C,D,E are in quadrant I; E=(9,2√3). Which listed OA is possible?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: The height of E is $\sqrt3s/2$, where s is the side length.
steps: Thus s=4. If A is the left endpoint of AF, E is 3s/2=6 units to its right, so A=(3,0). All four upper vertices then have positive x coordinates.
The reflected orientation instead gives A=(11,0), also possible. Of the listed lengths 2,3,4,1, only 3 is possible.
problems.note: The geometry itself allows OA=3 or 11; the question asks which listed value can occur.

problems.title: Translate a parabola
problems.question: Translate y=x²−2x+3 by vector (3,5). Find the new equation.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.

problems.title: Reflect points in vertical lines
problems.question: Reflect (0,2) in x=−3 to get A, and (−1,0) in x=2 to get B. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Reflection in $x=c$ sends $(x,y)$ to $(2c-x,y)$; distance $=\sqrt{\Delta x^2+\Delta y^2}$.

problems.title: The tens digit of a large power
problems.question: Find the tens digit of 2015^2022−2022.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: The last two digits are the residue modulo 100.
steps: 15² ends in 25, and multiplying 25 by 15 gives a number ending in 75, then multiplying 75 by 15 gives 25. Even positive powers of 15 therefore end in 25.
The exponent 2022 is even. Subtracting a number ending in 22 leaves last two digits 03. The tens digit is 0.

problems.title: Absolute values and periodicity
problems.question: Which of sin|x| and cos|x| is periodic?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The cosine function has period 2π. Suppose sin|x| had positive period T. On positive inputs periodicity forces T to be a multiple of 2π.
But at x=−π/2 the value is 1, while at x+T=T−π/2>0 the value is −1. This contradiction rules out every such period.

problems.title: Identify a decreasing function
problems.question: Which decreases on (π/6,π/2): sin x, −2/x, 0.8^(−x), or log base (2−√3) of x?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: A logarithm with base between 0 and 1 decreases on positive inputs.
steps: sin x increases on this interval. The derivative of −2/x is 2/x²>0. The exponential 0.8^(−x)=(1.25)^x increases.
Since 0<2−√3<1, the logarithm decreases.

problems.title: A trapezoid side as a vector
problems.question: AD∥BC, AD=30,BC=20; vectors AD=a, AB=b. Express CD.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: C=A+b+(2/3)a and D=A+a. Subtraction gives CD=(1/3)a−b.

problems.title: A median intersects an angle bisector
problems.question: AM is a median, BN an angle bisector, K their intersection, AB:BC=3:2. Find area(BMK)/area(ABC).
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Angle bisector theorem $AN:NC=3:2$; triangle areas sharing a base scale with height.
steps: Assign vertex masses A=2,C=3,B=3, so M has mass 6. Then AK:KM=6:2=3:1.
K has one quarter of A’s height above BC. Also BM=BC/2. Thus the area fraction is (1/4)(1/2)=1/8.

problems.title: Place a rational number between logarithms
problems.question: Which of 7/3,5/4,11/5,3/2 lies between log₃5 and log₂3?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Both comparisons hold after squaring: 25<27 and 8<9. Hence 3/2 lies inside. The other choices are outside (the endpoints are approximately 1.465 and 1.585).

problems.title: Vectors must always form an acute angle
problems.question: Find all a for which (x,a,0) and (x−a,1,a−2) have an acute angle for every real x.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Acute angle requires positive dot product: $x^2-ax+a>0$ for every x.
steps: Complete the square: (x−a/2)²+a−a²/4. Its minimum must be positive, so a(4−a)>0, giving 0<a<4.
For these a the first vector is nonzero; the second always has its second coordinate 1, so the angle is defined.

problems.title: Change the base of logarithms
problems.question: If log₄125=a, find log₂₅8.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: a=3 ln5/(2 ln2). Therefore log₂₅8=3 ln2/(2 ln5)=9/(4a).

problems.title: A semicircle outside a larger semicircle
problems.question: A small semicircle has diameter 1, which is a horizontal chord of a semicircle of diameter 2. Find the small region outside the larger semicircle, as drawn.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Sector area $=R^2\theta/2$ (radians); circular segment = sector minus triangle.
steps: The small semicircle has area π/8. The unit-radius larger circle’s chord of length 1 subtends 60°=π/3.
The overlapping circular cap has area π/6−√3/4. It is contained in the small semicircle. Subtract it: π/8−π/6+√3/4=√3/4−π/24.

problems.title: A quadratic in an exponential
problems.question: Solve 9^(x+0.5)−3^(x+1)−1=0.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: 3t²−3t−1=0 gives t=(3±√21)/6. Keep only the positive root.

problems.title: Rhombus area from its inradius
problems.question: A rhombus has inradius 2 and acute angle α with sin α=3/4. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Cancel s>0 to get s sinα=2r=4. Thus s=16/3. Area=2rs=4×16/3=64/3.

problems.title: Sum of two square roots of sine
problems.question: Solve √(1+sin x)+√(1−sin x)=√3.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Thus |cos x|=1/2, giving x=kπ±π/3. Both original square roots are nonnegative, so these solutions all satisfy the original equation.

problems.title: Indices of an arithmetic progression
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression with nonzero difference, k+p=14 and 2aₖ+a₄=aₚ+2a₇. Find positive integers k,p.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The a₁ terms cancel. Equating coefficients of d gives 2(k−1)+3=(p−1)+12, so 2k−p=10.
Together with k+p=14 this gives k=8,p=6.

problems.title: Perpendicular medians in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC; medians AM,CN meet at D at right angles. BNDM has area 4. Find the triangle perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: The median direction vectors are (3u/2,v/2) and (−3u/2,v/2). Their zero dot product gives v=3u.
The quadrilateral BNDM occupies one third of triangle ABC, since it consists of two of the six equal-area small median triangles. Thus area ABC=12.
Area ABC=uv=3u², so u=2,v=6. Base AC=4 and equal sides are √40=2√10.

problems.title: Work rate with an improvement
problems.question: The first worker makes k parts in 4 hours. The second makes m more parts per hour. How long for the second to make a parts?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Divide the required a parts by the second rate: a/(k/4+m)=4a/(k+4m) hours. The physical rate must be positive.

problems.title: A bisector and a circle in a right triangle
problems.question: C=90°, AD bisects A. A circle of radius √15 through A,C,D meets hypotenuse AB again at E, AE:EB=3:2. Find triangle area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
formulas: Power of B: $BA\cdot BE=BC\cdot BD$; bisector theorem $BD=BC\cdot AB/(AC+AB)$.
steps: Write AB=c,AC=b,BC=a. Since BE=2c/5, power of B gives 2c²/5=a²c/(b+c). Using a²=(c−b)(c+b) yields b=3c/5 and a=4c/5.
AC⊥CD, so AD is a diameter of the circle and AD=2√15. The bisector-length formula gives AD²=bc[1−a²/(b+c)²]=(9/20)c².
Thus c²=400/3. The area ab/2=(6/25)c²=32.

problems.title: Maximize profit over a whole number of products
problems.question: Each product earns 7.5 million GEL. First cost is 1.3 million; each next costs 0.7 million more. How many products maximize total profit?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, then check the conditions of the question.
steps: Check the adjacent integers: P(9)=30.6 and P(10)=30.5 million. Because the parabola opens downward, 9 is the global integer maximum.
